title: Every first breath, first dawn and first step began with Him
subtitle: Al-Mubdi': the One who begins creation and starts every beginning
intro: Al-Mubdi' (الْمُبْدِئُ) means The Originator, the One who begins: He brought creation into being the first time, when there was nothing, and He is the source of every beginning since. Your life had a first moment, and it was His. That means a new start is always in His hands, however many times you have failed before.

root.sense: Bad' means to begin, to start a thing for the first time, and mabda' is a starting point or origin. Al-Mubdi' is the One with whom every first time starts: the first creation, the first human, the first day of every life.

row.title: My story is already written off
sub: I have used up my chances

row.title: He is the One who begins
sub: starting from nothing is His way

knowing: There was a time when you were not a thing worth mentioning (76:1). No body, no name, no memory. {idea}Al-Mubdi' is the One who took that nothing and made it a beginning{/idea}. He did the same for the heavens and the earth, the first human, and every kind of creature, with no help and no prior material.

Human beings start things too, but always in the middle of a story that was already running: with tools already made, in a world already there, with a body already given. Only Allah begins in the true sense. Every other beginning is a continuation of His.

The Quran almost always mentions this name with its partner: it is He who begins creation and then repeats it (85:13, 10:4). His beginning is the proof of His power to return what He began. But beginning is a mercy on its own: {reward}nothing good in your life started without Him starting it{/reward}.
seeing: Travel through the land and look at how He began creation (29:20). The Quran sends you out to look at beginnings: a seed splitting, a chick breaking its shell, the first light on the horizon. Scientists still argue about how life first began. The believer knows Who began it, and keeps looking with wonder.

When the angel told Zakariyya he would have a son in his old age, Allah answered his astonishment by pointing to his own first beginning: it is easy for Me, for I created you before, when you were nothing (19:9). {reward}The One who began you can begin anything for you{/reward}.
trusting: Failure often feels final. A marriage ends, a business folds, a habit you swore off comes back again. {trap}You start to believe your story has no new chapters left{/trap}. Knowing Al-Mubdi' breaks that belief. He began you from less than this. He can begin a new chapter for you from where you are now, however little is left.

So begin small, and begin today: one prayer on time, one honest conversation, one step back toward Him. You do not have to fix the past first. The first revelation itself began with a command to read in the name of your Lord who created (96:1). Starting in His name is how every good beginning works.
loving: Everyone remembers who gave them their start: the teacher who believed in them, the boss who took a chance. Al-Mubdi' gave you your very first start, existence itself, before you could ask or earn it. {reward}Love for Him begins when you realize He chose to begin you{/reward}.
now: It is the first of January, or the first day after the rehab clinic, or the first morning in a new city where you know no one. Everything feels fragile and unfamiliar. Say Bismillah over this new day: the One who began the heavens and the earth is the One who began this morning for you.
old: I think a fresh start is only for people who have not failed as much as I have.
new: Al-Mubdi' begins from nothing, so He can begin something new with me today.
try: Choose one small good habit you have abandoned and begin it again today, saying Bismillah as you start it.

dua.text: Ya Mubdi', You began me when I was nothing. Begin for me today a new chapter of obedience, and do not let my past failures close the door You have opened.
dua.note: Call on Him by this name at any beginning: a new day, a new job, a new attempt at repentance.

pairs.why: He begins creation and He repeats it; the first creation is the proof of the second.
Al-Mubdi' is the One who begins; Al-Badi' stresses that the beginning copied no model.
Al-Khaliq measures and brings into being at every moment; Al-Mubdi' is about the very first time.

faq.a: Al-Mubdi' means the One who begins or originates: He brought creation into being the first time, from nothing. Every beginning in the universe, including your own life, started with Him.

faq.q: Is Al-Mubdi' mentioned in the Quran?
faq.a: The name is taken from verses describing Allah's action, such as 85:13, which says it is He who begins and repeats, and 10:4, 29:19 and 30:27, which say He begins creation and then repeats it. It is in the well-known list of names narrated by at-Tirmidhi.

faq.q: What is the difference between Al-Mubdi' and Al-Mu'id?
faq.a: Al-Mubdi' begins creation the first time; Al-Mu'id brings it back again, after death, for the resurrection. The Quran pairs them so that the first creation becomes evidence for the second.
